SMTO-EXE-0020 — SMTO is trying a saved, proven way to do this first

GUID: 3e0d98e4-439f-4f3c-a16f-a1b4f5646181
Slug: verified-execution-fast-path-available
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO has a saved procedure that already worked for this kind of request, so it held back a web search to try that first. This is only a notice; it doesn't mean the work already ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task keep going and watch for its result. SMTO tries the saved procedure first and only searches the web if that is still needed.
  2. If you want SMTO to look things up fresh instead, open Settings › Agent behavior › Fast Cache and select Remove on the matching entry. Saved procedures in Fast Cache are what lead SMTO to hold back the web search.

What success looks like

  • The task finishes with a result, either from the saved procedure or after a web search.

If it still fails

  • If the task stops making progress, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't treat this notice as a sign the work already ran.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The discovery policy deferred a web search/read because a refreshed verified Fast Cache execution path is pending for this goal; this is a routing notice, not an execution result.

What this means

  • The discovery policy found a refreshed verified execution path pending and deferred a web search/read request until that path is considered. This is a routing notice, not proof that the task already executed. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • The discovery policy found a refreshed verified execution path pending and deferred a web search/read request until that path is considered. This is a routing notice, not proof that the task already executed.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the current verified-path hint and its prerequisites; a cached procedure is distinct from a receipt of this run's execution.

How to fix it

  • No corrective action is required for this informational outcome.
  • No fix is needed. The routing.discovery_policy guard returned a recoverable retry so the verified Fast Cache path is evaluated first; any actual execution is recorded separately. To force fresh discovery, remove the matching entry in Settings › Agent behavior › Fast Cache.

Retry and execution caution

  • This condition does not authorize a retry or require an automatic action.

How to verify the fix

  • The owning runtime evaluates the verified path under current policy and records any actual execution separately.

What not to do

  • Do not turn this status into an automatic retry or a new execution request.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
